title: Money & currency
body:
Luxembourg uses the euro (€). ATMs are widely available in the city centre, and contactless card payment is the norm — the market stalls and smaller Grund bars are the main places cash still helps.

Luxembourg is one of Europe's more expensive capitals: a financial-hub economy pushes hotel and restaurant prices above nearby Belgium or France.

title: Budget & daily costs
intro: Per-person estimates for a mid-range trip. Public transport is free nationwide, so the biggest daily swing is food. Sights are cheap individually (€5–13 each) — the itinerary below visits at most one or two paid sights a day.

items.label: Lodging, per night (per room)
items.note: ≈€140/night is a typical mid-range Luxembourg City rate; confirm against your actual booking.

items.label: Food & drink, per day
items.note: Market lunch + casual dinner; a sit-down Luxembourgish dinner runs toward the high end.

items.label: Local transport, per day
items.note: Buses, trams and 2nd-class trains are free nationwide (since 1 Mar 2020).

items.label: Sights & activities, per day
items.note: Bock Casemates €11, MNHA €7, Musée Dräi Eechelen €7 (or €12 combined), Villa Vauban €5 — the plan visits one or two of these most days.

items.label: Vianden half-day (castle + transit)
items.note: Castle admission only — the train/bus connection is free nationwide transit.
